description: Honest parameter-free test of whether the Whipple toroidal amplitude at the physical forced windings (mu,nu)=(1/2,d-1/2) reproduces the observed even/odd binding ratio (deuteron, d=2). No fit; explicit NULL if no parameter-free match. auditOnly.

results.factor2_finding: The deuteron 2/|C(d=2)| = 3.33 ≈ observed 3.373 (1.2%) is a COINCIDENCE, not a derived factor. The hypothesis B_even/B_odd = A/|C(d=A)| fails badly for A≥3 (446% off at A=3, 1644% at A=4) because |C| collapses (0.60, 0.24, 0.069) while the observed ratios stay O(2-7). The fixed constant 3.33 also matches ⁴He (0.3%) but not ³H/³He — i.e. it hits the two N=Z cases only, a fixed number matching 2 of 4 points, not a law. NOT wired (anti-fit / no-seventh-ansatz discipline).
results.note: Only the deuteron (d=2, single pn bond) has a clean axial distance; heavier isotopes lack a single d and are reported unscored for the amplitude test. The factor-2 falsification uses the falsifiable hypothesis ratio = A/|C(d=A)| regardless of whether d=A is exact.

verdict: NULL (honest, not a fit): the bare Whipple constant |C(nu,mu)| and the raw toroidal amplitude ratio at the physical forced windings (mu,nu)=(1/2,d-1/2) do NOT reproduce the observed even/odd binding ratio (deuteron B_even/B_odd) to 5% under any parameter-free combination {C, 1/C, amp, 1/amp}. The Whipple identification is mathematically exact but its BARE amplitude is not the observable ratio -- the binding-closure gap must supply the E0-scaled, many-body dressing between the dimensionless toroidal amplitude and the MeV even/odd split. This sharpens (does not close) the gap; nothing is fitted or wired. FURTHER: the tempting deuteron 2/|C| match is FALSIFIED as a derived factor — ratio = A/|C(d=A)| fails 446%/1644% at A=3/4 (see factor2_generalization_falsification); the factor-2 is a coincidence, explicitly NOT wired.
